label: Office-document sweep + archive listing. Two findings here are serious enough to act on before any further model work.

office_sweep_final.orphan_note: Most OFFICE_XLSX 'orphans' are the agent correctly citing cell addresses in the ORIGINAL .xlsx after it bypassed my broken .txt dump and read xl/worksheets/*.xml directly. That is better provenance than the dump, not worse.

CRITICAL_FINDING_1_BRIER_FLOOR_IS_NON_BI.severity: HIGH — a published quality gate does not test what it claims to test
CRITICAL_FINDING_1_BRIER_FLOOR_IS_NON_BI.claim_a: The gate uses a Brier <= 0.22 publishability floor.
CRITICAL_FINDING_1_BRIER_FLOOR_IS_NON_BI.claim_b: At base rate 0.69 a ZERO-SKILL constant forecast yields Brier 0.2139 < 0.22. The floor is passed by a model with no predictive power whatsoever.
CRITICAL_FINDING_1_BRIER_FLOOR_IS_NON_BI.action: Replace the absolute Brier floor with a skill-score floor (Brier Skill Score vs base rate), which is zero for a constant forecast and cannot be gamed by the base rate.

CRITICAL_FINDING_2_ECE_FAILS_ON_DEPLOYED.detail: Deployed v5.2.7 ECE 0.1089 vs floor 0.05 — it FAILS its own floor — while the pooled sample clears. The aggregate number hides the deployed regression.
CRITICAL_FINDING_2_ECE_FAILS_ON_DEPLOYED.related: Best single version (v5.2.7) Brier 0.2489 on n=353; Brier after perfect recalibration ~0.244 on n=1663, i.e. recalibration buys almost nothing.
CRITICAL_FINDING_2_ECE_FAILS_ON_DEPLOYED.action: Gate on the DEPLOYED version, not the pooled sample.

CRITICAL_FINDING_3_MURPHY_DECOMPOSITION_.detail: At 10 equal-width bins rel - res + unc = 0.2438 but Brier = 0.2106; within-bin residual ~0.033. The terms are not additive at that bin count, so using the decomposition as a reconciliation check is unsound.
CRITICAL_FINDING_3_MURPHY_DECOMPOSITION_.action: Either use many more bins / adaptive binning, or stop treating rel-res+unc == Brier as a validation check.

CLV_INTEGRITY.denominator_contamination: System CLV 23.2% [0.212,0.253] counts MATCHED_CLOSE failures as non-beats; decided-only CLV 40.8% [0.377,0.441]. Both must be published. Floor is 52.4% at -110. Neither clears it.
CLV_INTEGRITY.surface_contamination: ELITE's canUseClvLedger gates a client-only localStorage manual bet log with NO code path to the platform's own graded picks (docs/data/CARDS_PROOF_LADDER.md:69-73). Any CLV from that surface is not platform CLV.
CLV_INTEGRITY.contested_benchmark: The market-efficiency assumption behind CLV is itself contested (1710.02824, 2008.01485). The build plan's cheapest high-value action is: does CLV actually correlate with better Brier in GSE's own settled picks? If not, the benchmark needs revisiting.

MARKET_LINES_AS_FEATURES_unresolved_and_.claim_a: nflfastR/Baldwin: adding the pre-game point spread to the WP model cuts log loss 0.52 -> 0.44 and error 27% -> 23%. Spread as a feature is beneficial.
MARKET_LINES_AS_FEATURES_unresolved_and_.claim_b: World-Class audit: incorporating closing lines or near-game odds as features destroys CLV measurement (target leakage); the pure performance engine must stay decoupled.
MARKET_LINES_AS_FEATURES_unresolved_and_.status: UNRESOLVED. This is not academic — it decides whether the engine may use the single most informative available feature.
MARKET_LINES_AS_FEATURES_unresolved_and_.note: The de-vigged close over 5,281 NFL games 2006-2025 is already calibrated: pooled Brier 0.2106, adaptive ECE 0.0126, and isotonic/Platt/beta beat identity by <= 0.0005. Market moneyline recalibration is therefore KILLED for the engine, and bridge-model.ts rebuild is prohibited (stated Brier 0.2237 vs spread-bucket 0.2120 on 285 sealed 2025 games).
